title: Drowning
summary: Use a safe rescue, give rescue breaths promptly, then CPR and an AED if breathing is not normal.
sources: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care — Drowning
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 — First Aid
actions: Do not enter dangerous water unless trained and equipped. Reach, throw a flotation aid, or use a safe rescue method.
Once on a firm surface, call emergency services and check responsiveness and breathing.
If unresponsive and not breathing normally, open the airway and give 2 effective rescue breaths, then begin cycles of 30 chest compressions and 2 breaths. Use an AED as soon as available.
If unresponsive but breathing normally, place in the recovery position, keep warm, and monitor continuously.
Seek medical assessment for persistent cough, breathing trouble, unusual sleepiness, or any loss of consciousness after submersion.
prohibitions: Do not endanger yourself by entering unsafe water.
Do not use abdominal thrusts to remove water.
Do not assume the person is safe because they initially look well.

emergencyCall.text: Any person rescued from water with abnormal breathing, reduced responsiveness, or ongoing symptoms needs emergency assessment.
